fullPassage: It is thanks to the technology involved in Web 2.0 that people may now actively engage with internet content. If at first we had to make do with witty PowerPoint attachments, now we can create and upload our own clips, gifs, selfies, etc. For example, YouTube hosts countless videos uploaded by members of the public. Anyone can produce and post a homemade video on YouTube, just as they may post a scene they themselves have extracted from a professionally made film or a TV series or even create a compilation of different scenes by a certain actor or on a particular topic. And much of what people upload on YouTube appears to be actually humorous in intent. Of course, these compilations beg a number of questions. They are not only divorced from the contexts in which they first appeared, but they are consumed in a different era, and this must surely have an effect on the way they are received. Similarly, Facebook also allows users to upload and share things with others, and undoubtedly here too, much of what is created, uploaded, and shared is humorous. The pattern seems to be that first I, as an individual, find something funny online that may make me laugh or smile. Second, as I am alone with my laughter, I decide to share that same object of amusement with others, many of whom will display a "like" and possibly forward the message to others who will in turn do likewise. So by forwarding, sharing, and stimulating "likes" in others, we somehow create a new form of collective online laughter.

If at first we had to make do with witty PowerPoint attachments, now we can create and upload our own clips, gifs, selfies, etc. For example, YouTube hosts countless videos uploaded by members of the public. Anyone can produce and post a homemade video on YouTube, just as they may post a scene they themselves have extracted from a professionally made film or a TV series or even create a compilation of different scenes by a certain actor or on a particular topic. And much of what people upload on YouTube appears to be actually humorous in intent. Of course, these compilations beg a number of questions. They are not only divorced from the contexts in which they first appeared, but they are consumed in a different era, and this must surely have an effect on the way they are received. Similarly, Facebook also allows users to upload and share things with others, and undoubtedly here too, much of what is created, uploaded, and shared is humorous. The pattern seems to be that first I, as an individual, find something funny online that may make me laugh or smile. Second, as I am alone with my laughter, I decide to share that same object of amusement with others, many of whom will display a "like" and possibly forward the message to others who will in turn do likewise. So by forwarding, sharing, and stimulating "likes" in others, we somehow create a new form of collective online laughter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 actively와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: actively(능동적으로) ↔ passively(수동적으로)
det.analysis:
❌ ① eagerly — 열성적으로 (의미축 다름: 태도)
❌ ② directly — 직접적으로 (의미축 다름: 방식)
❌ ③ openly — 공개적으로 (의미축 다름)
✅ ④ passively — 수동적으로 (반의어) ←정답

det.analysis:

questions.passage:
(A) Anyone can produce and <u>post</u> a homemade video on YouTube.

(B) He tied his horse to the wooden <u>post</u> standing beside the gate.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 post의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 홈메이드 영상을 올리다 → '게시하다' (B) 말을 나무 기둥에 매다 → '기둥'
det.analysis:
❌ ① 기둥 — 게시하다 (A와 B가 뒤바뀜)
❌ ② 우편 — 게시하다 (A는 '우편'이 아님)
✅ ③ 게시하다 — 기둥 ←정답
❌ ④ 게시하다 — 직위 (B는 '직위'가 아닌 '기둥')

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"a collection of things, such as songs, scenes, or writings, put together from different sources into one work"

det.korean: 여러 출처에서 모아 하나로 엮은 모음 → compilation(편집물, 모음집)
det.analysis:
❌ ① attachment — 첨부물 (정의와 다름)
❌ ② context — 맥락 (정의와 무관)
❌ ③ era — 시대 (정의와 무관)
✅ ④ compilation — 편집물, 모음집, compilation of different scenes ←정답
det.tip: compilation = 편집물, 모음집 (여러 장면을 모아 엮은 것)

questions.passage: For example, YouTube hosts countless videos __________ (upload) by members of the public.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사(videos)를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사이므로 upload → uploaded (수동, ~에 의해 올려진)
det.analysis: countless videos __________ by members → videos를 수식하는 분사. '대중에 의해 올려진'이므로 수동 과거분사 → uploaded
det.tip: upload(올리다) → uploaded (과거분사: 올려진, videos uploaded by ~)

questions.passage: So by __________ (forward), sharing, and stimulating "likes" in others, we somehow create a new form of collective online laughter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 전치사 by 뒤이며 sharing, stimulating과 병렬을 이루므로 forward → forwarding (동명사)
det.analysis: by __________, sharing, and stimulating → 전치사 by + 동명사, 뒤의 sharing·stimulating과 병렬 → forwarding
det.tip: by + 동명사 = ~함으로써 / forward → forwarding (sharing, stimulating과 병렬)
